## 3. Integration notes

- Modules follow the exact kernel interface: `@module(...)` on a `Module` subclass,
  `enterprise.platform_kernel` imports, `initialize`/`health_check`/`shutdown`,
  `set_event_bus`, `HealthStatus`, event emission via `EventBus`.
- All four are **dependency-free** (stdlib only). External integrations (real
  Telegram/Discord HTTP, nat. tests use injected fakes) never run in CI tests.
- `task_harness` and `semantic_memory` persist to SQLite / a vector index.
  All test IO uses `tmp_path` — **no fake data and no repo pollution**.
- `gateway` emits `gateway.message.sent`; `skill_factory` emits
  `skill.created/updated/evolved`; `semantic_memory` emits `memory.doc.indexed/query`;
  `task_harness` emits `task.created/state_changed` — all guard a `None` event bus.

## 4. What adds R (keep) / what to drop

- **Keep**: dependency-free cores (no install burden, tests stay fast/hermetic);
  injectable adapters (opener/fake-embedder) for external services; strict
  `Module` lifecycle conformance → auto-discovers with zero kernel edits.
- **Drop/avoid**: pulling in `croniter`/`sentence-transformers`/`python-telegram-bot`
  as hard deps — pure-Python equivalents keep the platform self-contained.
